content: embedded-graphics-framebuf 0.5.0 only ships FrameBufferBackend impls for fixed-size arrays ([C;N]/&mut [C;N]), not Vec<C> (and can't be added downstream due to orphan rules - both the trait and Vec are foreign). Solution: a local newtype (HeapBuffer(Vec<Rgb565>)) implementing FrameBufferBackend, which keeps FrameBuffer565's resolution a runtime parameter instead of a compile-time const generic. Also: DrawTargetExt::clipped(&area) does NOT translate coordinates into area-relative space, it only clips - widgets must still draw in absolute framebuffer coordinates offset by area.top_left.

Bash tool cwd persists across calls, so a cd into a worktree silently retargets every later git command - a merge then reports Already up to date because it ran on the branch being merged. Use absolute paths or cd back explicitly.

core has no core::time::Instant; introduced platform::Instant (a u64-microseconds newtype with saturating_duration_since + Add<Duration>) that every Clock impl converts to at the trait boundary. HostClock now records a std::time::Instant epoch at construction and reports elapsed micros since it. Also moved std::thread::sleep out of run() entirely into Clock::sleep(&self, Duration) -- run.rs:93 rationale block flipped from 'thread::sleep works on every target' to 'no_std has no std::thread, so the platform decides what blocking means'. run.rs:411's std::error::Error mention was pure doc-comment wording (StubFlushError only ever derived Debug) -- reworded, no code changed.

cc::Build (per-file compile + incremental ar) avoids the previous attempt's 'argument list too long' - that came from a single giant gcc invocation with hundreds of source files on the command line, not from any real toolchain limit. Any future C cross-compile probe should default to cc::Build or an explicit response-file Makefile, never a hand-rolled shell one-liner.

panic-halt's bare loop{} silently converts any panic into what looks like a total, USB-independent hang. The real bug (CONTROL_BUF too small - see parallel investigation's comment) panicked inside usb_task's poll on core0's cooperative executor, not inside the USBCTRL_IRQ ISR; because panic-halt never unwinds, Executor::run() never regained control to poll ANY other task, which starved watchdog_feed_task and the old async-Timer safety_net_task right along with USB. That is why a 180s 'independent' safety net never fired even after 15+ minutes - it was never USB-independent in the first place, since it shared an executor with the thing that panicked. Fixed both: grew CONTROL_BUF 64B->256B (root cause - config.product needs 78 bytes as UTF-16LE, only 64 were available), and replaced panic_halt with a #[panic_handler] that calls reset_to_usb_boot() directly so any FUTURE panic self-recovers in ~0s instead of relying on the 8s hardware watchdog or wedging forever. General lesson for this board: a bare halt-loop panic handler is actively hostile to unattended iteration on a target with no RTT/probe - it makes every panic indistinguishable from a genuine deadlock, which is the expensive kind of bug to diagnose blind.

BTstack's btstack_run_loop_embedded.c is gated on HAVE_EMBEDDED_TICK vs HAVE_EMBEDDED_TIME_MS at compile time (mutually exclusive, #error if both defined). btstack_config.h in this spike already set HAVE_EMBEDDED_TIME_MS, so hal_tick_init/hal_tick_set_handler/hal_tick_get_tick_period_in_ms were NEVER CALLED even before this bead - confirmed by grep, all three call sites in btstack_run_loop_embedded.c are inside '#ifdef HAVE_EMBEDDED_TICK' blocks that were compiled out. Deleted them rather than leaving dead stubs, per the bead's ask. Also: nestable hal_cpu_disable_irqs/enable_irqs needs a depth counter, not a save/restore of PRIMASK's prior state - BTstack's own call sites (run loop + hci.c/l2cap.c critical sections) always pair disable/enable 1:1 with no interleaving from other code, so a simple 0<->N counter (only the 0->1 transition masks, only the 1->0 transition unmasks) is sufficient and correct; verified by reading every call site, not by fuzzing actual nesting on hardware. Also: hal_cpu_enable_irqs_and_sleep must NOT do a real WFI unless the core actually has an unmasked periodic interrupt source configured on its own NVIC - core1 here has none, so WFI would sleep forever and silently kill the run loop's idle path. This would have been a nasty one to debug blind (looks identical to 'BTstack is stuck', not obviously a sleep-forever bug) if not caught by reading hal_cpu_enable_irqs_and_sleep's call site in btstack_run_loop_embedded_execute_once before implementing it.

embassy-usb's class.write_packet().await BLOCKS (backpressure) when nothing is draining the CDC bulk endpoint - it does not error on host disconnect. A debug console loop that reads-then-writes-then-loops (like console_task here) will therefore hold a stale snapshot across any disconnect and deliver it late, then resume live, on reconnect. Two backlogged lines draining back-to-back at reconnect (timestamped within ~100ms of each other) is indistinguishable, if you only look at PRINTED deltas, from either a burst or a stall in the thing being measured. Any future debug telemetry over a blocking CDC/serial channel needs to be judged skeptically against this artifact before blaming the subsystem it's reporting on - prefer non-blocking/dropping writes (or a channel that can't back up) for anything used to diagnose timing bugs.

RP2350's pico-sdk hardware_gpio/gpio.c uses a NEW-to-RP2350 'GPIO coprocessor' fast path (gpioc_bit_oe_put etc, a CP0 custom instruction) not present on RP2040. A Rust-owned binary that bypasses pico-sdk's own crt0/runtime_init (as this one deliberately does, per the ADR) never enables CP0 access, so the FIRST call to gpio_set_dir/gpio_set_pulls (cyw43_init's WL_REG_ON pin config) takes a UsageFault/NOCP (CFSR 0x80000). Fix: OR M33 CPACR (0xE000ED88, standard ARMv8-M address) with 0x3 (CP0 full access) once per core, before any pico-sdk GPIO call - this replicates pico-sdk's own runtime_init_per_core_enable_coprocessors() (one register write), not its whole init-table walk. Confirmed via a HardFault handler dumping PC/LR/CFSR over CDC: PC landed exactly inside gpioc_bit_oe_put. This will bite pico-link-xkp.2 (TinyUSB dcd) too if TinyUSB's RP2350 dcd also uses any GPIO/hardware coprocessor fast path - worth checking there before re-deriving this.

cyw43-driver's LICENSE.RP (not its default LICENSE, which is non-commercial-only) is the applicable one here - it grants unrestricted commercial use as long as the software runs 'solely with... RP2040 or any other semiconductor device produced by [Raspberry Pi Ltd]'. RP2350 qualifies (same Licensor). So linking cyw43-driver is fine for Pico Link commercially, AS LONG AS this firmware only ever targets Raspberry Pi silicon - flag this if the product roadmap ever considers a non-RP MCU.

bd show exits 0 for a nonexistent bead ID and only prints an error line, so exit status cannot validate an ID. Use bd show ID --json and check that the result parses as an array whose first element has the expected id - the miss returns an object with an error key instead.

nm check (day-1, per bead) on the ui-ffi staticlib for thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf: memcpy/memset/memmove/memcmp and every __aeabi_* symbol from compiler_builtins are WEAK (W), not strong (T) -- they yield to newlib's strong definitions at final link with zero collision risk, no --allow-multiple-definition and no objcopy --localize-symbol needed. The only undefined (U) symbols found were _critical_section_1_0_acquire/_release (from embedded-alloc's LlffHeap, which needs a critical_section::Impl registered) -- addressing with a hand-rolled cpsid/cpsie primask impl in ui-ffi, not cortex-m-rt (forbidden by the bead).

the bead's ui-ffi target triple as literally written (thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf) fails final link against pico-sdk's build of this board with 'uses VFP register arguments, pico_link.elf does not' (every ui-ffi object file). pico-sdk builds this board's C code softfp (see its thumb/v8-m.main+fp/softfp object path -- hardware FPU instructions allowed, but integer registers for the calling convention), while Rust's ...eabihf target uses hardfloat (VFP register) argument passing -- an ABI mismatch, not a bug in the FFI surface itself. Fixed by switching ui-ffi's cross-compile target to thumbv8m.main-none-eabi (soft-float, no hf suffix) in firmware/CMakeLists.txt -- its calling convention (integer registers for float args) matches pico-sdk's softfp exactly, and it links clean. Also added 'rustup target add' as a build-command prefix since this target isn't installed by default.

heap fix (192KB) confirmed working on hardware. Flashed twice; both times the device settled into a stable, monotonically-incrementing heartbeat loop (11-19, then after a fresh reflash 5-15) with zero resets/crashes -- strong evidence the full pl_ui_create -> pl_ui_render -> pl_ui_input -> pl_ui_tick -> pl_ui_render sequence in main.c executes successfully on real hardware without faulting (a HardFault or alloc-error trap before the heartbeat loop would prevent it from ever being reached, let alone incrementing cleanly across two separate boots). Did not manage to capture the actual boot-banner/pl_ui_render sample-pixel diagnostic text over CDC in either attempt -- by the time the tty_fallback reader connects and DTR raises, TinyUSB's console ring buffer has already moved past those early lines (only ~1.5-5s of runtime, mostly consumed by the boot sleep_ms(1500)). This is a host-side capture-timing race, not a firmware issue; the absence of any crash/reset is itself sufficient evidence the FFI path worked. Continuing to stage 4 (ST7789 driver port) next.

full hardware pipeline (backlight -> RGB solid fills -> pl_ui_create -> input init -> render+blit loop) flashed and ran successfully, captured over CDC: 'panel: solid BLUE fill' / 'pl_ui_create OK' / 'pl_link_input_init OK' / 'frame 1: render=26624us blit=1008027us total=1034694us'. The ~1.008s blit is NOT a bug -- it is the expected DMA transfer time at the deliberately-conservative 1MHz SPI clock: 240*240*16 bits = 921,600 bits / 1e6 Hz = 0.9216s, matching the measurement almost exactly. This is why the bead says keep the clock low until CS framing is confirmed and NOT to bump it prematurely -- I have NOT bumped the clock, since confirming panel framing/colors requires a human (or webcam) looking at the actual panel, which I could not do in this environment (no camera capture CLI tool found on this Mac in this session). CDC output only ever captured a few lines per read due to a host-side timing race (tty_fallback connects a couple seconds after boot, missing the earliest banner/fill lines) -- not a firmware issue; every capture that did land showed clean, expected progression with zero crashes/resets across 3 separate flashes. HANDOFF TO ANDREAS: please visually confirm on the physical panel (or webcam) that the R/G/B fill sequence at boot shows correct, non-inverted colors in the right order, and that the joystick/buttons move the placeholder list's selection once the render loop starts. If colors are wrong, the bug is isolated to firmware/src/st7789.c (zero Rust involved in the fill sequence). Once framing is confirmed, ST7789_INIT_BAUDRATE_HZ in st7789.h can be raised (e.g. to 40-62MHz) to bring frame time down from ~1s to the tens-of-ms range.

the M1b panel renders correct GEOMETRY but wrong COLOUR. Orchestrator compared a settled webcam frame against the emulator headless PNG of the same root screen: empty background area is (8,16,32) near-black navy in the emulator and photographs as (167,248,245) on the panel - the brightest region in frame. Near-black cannot photograph as the brightest thing at any exposure, so inversion is established. Layout, text, rows and footer are pixel-correct, so the FFI seam, core rendering and the DMA blit are all proven RIGHT; the fault is confined to colour mapping in firmware/src/st7789.c. Channel order is NOT established - camera auto white balance swung warm between captures, so R-vs-B readings are untrustworthy while luminance is. The decisive test is the R/G/B solid-fill sequence with zero Rust in it, classified by chroma: red photographing as cyan means inversion, red as blue means channel order.

.claude/frontend-reviews-requirement.md was not the only dead frontend-review boilerplate - discovery.md also had a step-5 block appending supervisor names to .claude/frontend-supervisors.txt for a 'frontend reviews hook' that does not exist in .claude/hooks/, plus RAMS/WIG entries in its completion report and quality checklist. Deleting only the named file would have left dangling instructions. Removed all of it. .claude/ui-constraints.md (Tailwind/React/Base UI rules) is the same class of dead template boilerplate but was left in place: it is out of this bead's scope and is only injected for react/vue/svelte supervisors that will never be created here.

core/src/app.rs root screen is now a live devices list (LinkState/DeviceEntry/Command types), driven via App::set_link_state/add_device/clear_devices/poll_command, all committed and host-tested green. Next: extend ui-ffi with pl_ui_set_link_state/pl_ui_add_device/pl_ui_clear_devices/pl_ui_poll_command, then the C-side BTstack wiring.

the PATH arm-none-eabi-gcc (Homebrew formula, /opt/homebrew/bin) is missing newlib specs (nosys.specs etc) -- 'cannot read spec file nosys.specs'. The real toolchain is the gcc-arm-embedded CASK at /Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin -- configure CMake with -DPICO_TOOLCHAIN_PATH=/Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin. Worth adding to CLAUDE.md's firmware-build notes so it isn't rediscovered.

with the M2 build flashed, the board DOES enumerate USB CDC (picotool sees a USB serial connection, 0x2e8a:0x0009) yet cdc_reader.py claims the interface cleanly and reads ZERO bytes in 8 seconds, and the panel photographs at (22,20,21) - genuinely dark. Do NOT infer from enumeration that main() ran: pico-sdk stdio_usb services TinyUSB from a timer/IRQ context and with PICO_STDIO_USB_ENABLE_RESET_VIA_VENDOR_INTERFACE=1 that keeps running while main() is hung, so USB being up is fully consistent with a hang in the first lines of main(). What it does rule out is the measurement-artifact hypothesis: the capture path works and there is genuinely nothing being printed. The untested variables are not the BT code, which was already compiled out with the same symptom, but the two build-config changes that stayed in the binary either way - PICO_STACK_SIZE=0xC000 and the mere linking of pico_btstack_classic, pico_btstack_cyw43 and pico_cyw43_arch_threadsafe_background.

root cause of the CDC silence (coordinator identified, I verified): pico-sdk's stdio_usb gates ALL console output on DTR by default (stdio_usb_connected() -> tud_cdc_connected()), and tools/usb-console/cdc_reader.py cannot assert DTR on macOS (EACCES on the CDC-Communication interface, bead pico-link-4mc) -- so a healthy board was indistinguishable from a hung one, always zero bytes. Fix: PICO_STDIO_USB_CONNECTION_WITHOUT_DTR=1 in target_compile_definitions (firmware/CMakeLists.txt, committed 68d1285). VERIFIED on the M1b baseline (rebuilt in /tmp/pl-baseline-check with the flag added, not committed there -- throwaway checkout): cdc_reader.py now captures the real boot banner and FILL_HOLD/FILL_START markers. Console is now a trustworthy signal for the M2 bisection.

RAM layout check (arm-none-eabi-size + nm) on the full M2 build (BT linked, PICO_STACK_SIZE=0xC000): .bss ends at 0x2003589c, stack region is 0x20076000-0x20082000 -- about 263KB of headroom between them, no collision with the 192KB Rust heap arena or BTstack's static buffers. Stack size was never the cause of the dark panel.

memory-capture.sh's bd watchdog was ineffective in a way the temp-dir tests never showed: the lookup ran inside a command substitution, so kill -9 on bd left any grandchild holding the substitution's pipe open and the substitution blocked until the grandchild exited. Measured 60s against a bd that just sleeps, on the PRE-FIX hook too. Redirect the background command to a temp FILE and cat it after wait - then wait returns as soon as the direct child dies and the watchdog actually bounds the call.

one bd show ID --json costs ~0.85s on this board. That is the whole cost model for the memory-capture hook: 3 distinct beads is 2.4s, and 25 distinct would blow the 10s hook timeout. Memoising resolved IDs makes repeated beads free (6 invocations over 3 distinct beads = 2.6s, not 5.1s), and a loop budget that also caps the per-lookup watchdog hard-bounds the worst case at 7.2s regardless of batch size or a wedged daemon.

hooks on macOS must be written for bash 3.2 - no associative arrays. A memo cache is a newline-delimited key TAB value string read with while IFS read done <<< string. And a helper that mutates that cache must return its result in a GLOBAL, not on stdout: command substitution runs the function in a subshell and silently throws the cache away, which looks like the cache simply never hitting.

verify a hook by piping synthetic PostToolUse JSON to the script on stdin with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointed at a mktemp -d and the working directory INSIDE the repo, then assert on line count AND on the order of the content fields. Counting entries alone would have passed a fix that captured all three matches in the wrong order. The worktree copy of a hook is never the copy Claude Code runs, so this stdin harness is the only real verification available before merge.

the 1MHz SPI clock is not merely a speed wart, it makes INPUT EFFECTIVELY DEAD, reported by Andreas 2026-08-28 pressing the joystick with no response. firmware/src/input.c:57 takes ONE sample per call to pl_link_input_poll, and firmware/src/main.c:133 calls it once per superloop iteration. The debounce is an 8-sample shift register that only accepts a state change when all 8 agree, and input.c:8 still declares a 1ms sample interval - but the loop runs at total=1032746us per frame because the 240x240 blit takes 1.008s at 1MHz. One sample per 1.03s times 8 samples means a button must be held about 8.3 seconds to register. Raising the clock to 40-62MHz brings the frame to about 25ms and the same 8 samples to about 200ms. The complementary robust fix is to sample input on a timer or IRQ independently of the frame loop, so responsiveness never depends on render time again. This is also why pico-link-d7k could not be verified: the connect path was never going to respond to a human-length press.

the reason this could not be verified is now known and is not a bug in the command path. Input is sampled once per superloop iteration and the loop runs at about 1.03s per frame at the current 1MHz SPI clock, so the 8-sample debounce needs roughly 8.3 seconds of continuous hold before a press registers at all. See pico-link-14l. Re-test this bead only AFTER the clock bump lands, otherwise a negative result says nothing about the connect path.

orchestrator confirmed the board's state after the hang - macOS STILL enumerates it as 'Pico Link Audio Dongle' 2e8a:000c in SPUSBDataType, so the USB device is answering enumeration, while picotool sees no BOOTSEL device and control transfers time out. That pattern fits USB being serviced from interrupt/timer context while the main loop is wedged, rather than the whole chip being dead. It also sharpens the starvation hypothesis: if tud_task() is only pumped once per UI frame and that frame contains a blocking ~1s blit at the 1MHz SPI clock, then isochronous audio starting up is exactly the event that overruns the software FIFO. That makes bead pico-link-14l - the SPI clock bump - a dependency of M3's critical path, not merely a cosmetic follow-up. Recommended sequencing for whoever picks this up: land the clock bump and the timer-driven input sampling of pico-link-5am FIRST, so the superloop is no longer a one-second blocking cycle, then retry M3 streaming. Retrying M3 against a 1Hz superloop may just reproduce the same starvation.

main.c needed ZERO changes for this fix -- pl_link_input_poll's signature and semantics (drain up to max newly-debounced press edges, safe to call every superloop iteration) stayed identical; only what happens inside input.c changed (a pico-sdk repeating timer now drives sampling+debounce in IRQ context, feeding a lock-free SPSC ring buffer that poll drains). This means the anticipated main.c merge conflict with the M3 TinyUSB work should not materialize at all.

add_repeating_timer_us(-PL_INPUT_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_US, ...) with a NEGATIVE interval fires every 1ms measured from the previous scheduled time, not from when the callback finished -- keeps the sample rate exact regardless of callback duration. Positive would drift. The SPSC ring buffer (32 capacity, IRQ writes head/superloop writes tail) needs no locking: each index has exactly one writer, and RP2350 byte-sized volatile loads/stores are inherently atomic, so this is the standard lock-free single-producer/single-consumer pattern.

step 1 (confirming the timer-driven input fix on hardware) needs a human press and Andreas was asleep -- flashed the merged fix (build/pico_link.uf2, board confirmed on 0c310a4), captured console output twice (20s then 25s), and confirmed the superloop is alive (frame 61: render=25147us blit=1008024us total=1033178us at the still-unmodified 1MHz SPI clock) but there is no intent-received debug print, so a physical press is the only oracle -- there is no automated input path on real hardware (pico-link-d7k). Deferring this check to Andreas: press one direction once while tools/usb-console/cdc_reader.py --duration 20 --out <file> runs, per pico-link-5am's fix. Best done together with pico-link-d7k's connect-path check, AFTER the SPI clock bump below lands -- response will be tens of ms instead of ~1s. Proceeding to steps 2 (SPI clock) and 3 (colour), both camera+console verifiable without hands.

the byte-swap mechanism gap is resolved, not left as folklore. Computed both candidates for BACKGROUND=0x0884: bitwise inversion ~0x0884=0xF77B decodes to RGB(247,239,222) -- bright, warm, near-white, consistent with the 'bright near-inversion' actually observed pre-fix. Byte-swapping the two bytes gives 0x8408 -> RGB(132,130,66), a dark olive, NOT bright at all -- ruled out, as the bead suspected. Root cause: channel_config_set_bswap on a same-width (16-bit-to-16-bit) DMA transfer does not reorder the two bytes of each RGB565 value the way byte-swapping raw bytes would; it produces something numerically closer to bitwise inversion of the transferred pattern in this configuration. This was actually already documented in firmware/src/st7789.c:160-178's existing comment (predates this session, from the M1b/M2 bring-up) -- st7789_blit_framebuffer's bswap=false is correct, and the comment there already says the DMA path with bswap=true photographed as 'almost exactly the bitwise inversion (~value)' of reference colours, checked numerically. This session's contribution is closing the loop: computed the actual numbers and confirmed inversion (not byte-swap) is the right explanation.

step 3 colour test executed and PASSED. Added a temporary (now permanent-but-disabled, PL_DIAG_COLOR_TEST) diagnostic in firmware/src/main.c that blits half-panel BACKGROUND (0x0884) / half-panel pure white (0xFFFF) and halts before BT/UI init, so the pattern holds for one photograph. Webcam capture (flash+capture in one shell command) + numeric sampling (PIL/numpy on the crop) gave: BACKGROUND patch mean RGB~(128,183,243), channel spread ~115 (clearly saturated blue); white patch mean RGB~(207,214,221), channel spread ~14 (near-neutral). BACKGROUND is nowhere near white within the SAME frame -- the exposure-immune relative test the bead asked for is satisfied: colour is not washed out or inverted to white on this panel. The absolute brightness/blue-shift vs the emulator reference (92,165,233 vs core's 8,16,32) is still unexplained in absolute terms but was never the question this test was designed to answer -- plausibly still camera exposure on an emissive panel, as originally suspected, but that remains unconfirmed and is a separate question from 'is it broken', which this test answers no to.

first attempt MADCTL=0xA0 (MY|MV) flashed and webcam-verified clean/unshifted 90-degree rotation -- text reads correctly and CASET/RASET needed no offset change (square 240x240 panel). BUT the cable ends up at the TOP of frame when text is upright, not the right as required. Direct photo evidence: rotating the raw frame 90deg CW makes 'Pico Link'/'Scan for headphones'/'TV' read upright, and in that same rotated view the USB cable points toward the top of frame, buttons at bottom. Switching to the other pure-rotation MADCTL option, 0x60 (MX|MV), as the next hypothesis -- one variable per flash, per the anti-loop rule.

MADCTL=0x60 (MX|MV) flashed and webcam-verified -- ALSO a clean unshifted 90-degree rotation, text upright and readable, but cable ends up at the LEFT of frame when text is upright (not right, not top either -- different wrong side than 0xA0's cable-top). Both the two pure-90-rotation MADCTL options (0x60, 0xA0) now tested and both wrong. By elimination, since 4 MADCTL rotation values must map to 4 distinct cable-relative-to-upright-text positions (top/left/bottom/right), the answer is one of the two untested values: 0x00 (identity) or 0xC0 (MX|MY, 180, no transpose). Testing 0xC0 next; if wrong, 0x00 is the last remaining candidate by elimination.

the ground under this bead's blocker has shifted - the SPI clock bump landed on main as 8381c2b and the frame time went from 1.03s to 38.6ms (1MHz to 75MHz, the clk_peri/2 ceiling). The leading hypothesis for the streaming hang was that tud_task() is pumped once per UI frame while that frame blocks for about a second in the blit, starving USB exactly when isochronous audio starts. That starvation window is now roughly 27x smaller. Do NOT assume this fixes it - it may only move the failure - but the FIRST action on resuming this bead is to rebase the branch onto current main and simply retry streaming, before doing any further diagnosis. Also merged since this bead stopped: timer-driven input sampling (0c310a4) which moved debounce off the render loop entirely, and a display rotation change in flight on bd-pico-link-g7o. Expect a merge conflict in firmware/src/main.c from the rotation and input work; the branch itself is otherwise intact and its descriptors were verified byte-by-byte off the live device, so that work does not need redoing.

two things now need the SAME single human press, do them together. (1) the timer-driven input fix from pico-link-5am, merged as 0c310a4, is only build-verified plus Andreas's informal 'navigation works' before the rotation landed. (2) the input pin-to-intent remap from pico-link-g7o, merged as 52c6c53, rotated the mapping 180 degrees to match MADCTL 0xA0 and is completely unverified. Hold the board with the USB CABLE EXITING RIGHT - that is the orientation the display is now built for - then push the stick toward the top of the screen and confirm the selection moves UP, and left/right match what you see. Then press select on a discovered device and confirm PL_CMD_CONNECT appears in a cdc_reader.py capture, which is this bead's original acceptance. If up and down are swapped, the 180-degree remap was applied in the wrong direction and only the table in firmware/src/input.c needs flipping - the display is proven correct.

usb_audio.c, usb_descriptors.c/.h and tusb_config.h exist ONLY on bd-pico-link-cz0.4, not on main -- main.c on main has zero tud_task/audio call sites. Any bead touching M3 audio code must branch from cz0.4, not main, until M3 merges.

MADCTL 0x60 is IDENTITY on this panel (no rotation, no mirror) and 0x00 is a clean 90-degree-CCW rotation of it -- neither matches the textbook ST7789 assumption that 0x60/0xA0 are a 180-degree MV-transpose pair. The two MY-set candidates (0xA0, 0xC0) are NOT clean rotations at all: both render as a corrupted three-column-band image (~80px/~120px/~40px instead of 120/120), reproduced identically across two full 4-candidate cycles. Ruled out: stale address counter (reissuing CASET/RASET right after the MADCTL write made no difference) and a simple GRAM column offset (swept CASET x-offset 0/20/40/60/80, none cleaned it up). The defect tracks the MY bit specifically (both corrupted candidates have MY set, both clean candidates don't) -- looks like the classic ST7789-panel-in-oversized-GRAM row addressing quirk, but needs the RASET axis and/or larger offsets tested, not CASET at these values.

cbindgen 0.29.4 handles a Rust repr(C) union cleanly (PlEventPayload/PlCommandPayload -> C union), so the tagged-union FFI shape (version+tag+union payload) needed no header hand-editing or config beyond adding the new types to cbindgen.toml's export.include list.

ui-ffi could not run cargo test at all before this bead -- its unconditional no_std plus target-specific PRIMASK inline asm fails to even compile on host (panic=unwind without std). Added the same cfg_attr(not(test), no_std) escape hatch pico_link_core already uses (gating the critical-section impl, heap arena, and panic_handler behind cfg(not(test))) so cargo test -p ui-ffi now works: 8 new tests, all green. ui-ffi stays out of workspace default-members deliberately (see Cargo.toml comment), so bare cargo test at repo root is unaffected -- still 142. Flagging this for the orchestrator: the bead assumed a bare cargo test count rise; it's cargo test -p ui-ffi that rises instead.

u8g2-fonts 0.5.2 ships helvB18_tf and helvB24_tf, both usable within the design's ~20-26px hero band. Chose helvB24_tf, measured 25px cap height for all-caps words via get_rendered_dimensions_aligned in core/examples/hero_font_probe.rs. Raw glyph table cost: 6566 bytes (helvB24_tf) vs 3275 bytes (helvB12_tf, already linked). _tf glyph set includes ASCII digits.

pico-sdk's own hardware_watchdog.c (watchdog_enable/watchdog_reboot) claims scratch[4..7] for its own bookkeeping (a magic marker in [4], pc/sp handshake in [5..7]) -- so the bead's 8-register payload spec had to shrink to scratch[0..3], since this file calls watchdog_enable/watchdog_reboot on every panic and those calls would clobber [4..7]. That 4-register budget happens to fit exactly: magic, fault-or-PC address, line-number-or-CFSR, retry counter.

pico-sdk's __uninitialized_ram() macro (pico/platform/sections.h) places a variable in .uninitialized_data, a NOLOAD RAM section that pico_crt0/rp2350/memmap_default.ld puts before .data/.bss, and pico_crt0/crt0.S's zero loop only walks __bss_start__..__bss_end__ -- so it is untouched at boot, the C-first equivalent of the bead's original cortex-m-rt .uninit buffer. Confirmed post-link: s_panic_msg sits at 0x20000110, well below __bss_start__ at 0x200029e0.

pico-sdk's panic()/assert path is overridable per-target via -DPICO_PANIC_FUNCTION=<name> because pico_platform_panic/CMakeLists.txt adds panic.c as an INTERFACE source -- it compiles into whichever target links it and sees THAT target's compile definitions, no global add_definitions needed. Confirmed via objdump: panic() now disassembles as push{lr}; bl pl_panic_c_hook; bkpt. HardFault is overridden separately via the weak isr_hardfault symbol in pico_crt0/crt0.S (decl_isr_bkpt macro) -- confirmed the HardFault vector table word in the linked ELF points at isr_hardfault with the thumb bit set.

identity key resolved at selected_key()/with_selected_identity() time by scanning items, no stored key field needed on VerticalList itself -- avoids a whole class of key/index desync bugs since it derives from items+selected in one place.

core/examples/wizard_screenshots.rs's open_wizard() was stale since the E7 navigator change (Home became root) -- it sent one Select where three are now needed, so every fixture past 01_instructions silently captured the wrong screen/phase (e.g. 04a_connecting_acl.png actually showed the Instructions phase). Fixed it while verifying this bead since it was the only way to get a real screenshot of the wizard scan list; the previously-committed 04a-06g PNGs happened to already be correct (unchanged by the fix), only 02/02b/02c changed.

while running the hardware soak, another Claude session was concurrently holding/claiming the same board's CDC interface (process running tools/usb-console/cdc_reader.py from the MAIN checkout, not this worktree, plus at least one BOOTSEL/reflash cycle observed mid-session) -- this caused my own cdc_reader.py to hit EACCES (Access denied) and one libusb I/O Error crash. Two-readers-on-one-bus is exactly the hazard CLAUDE.md already warns about for cdc_reader/cdc_sender; it applies just as much across two AGENT SESSIONS as within one. A peer session identifying itself as rust-embedded-supervisor also messaged me mid-task asking for status/completion, consistent with a duplicate dispatch on this same bead. Orchestrator should avoid dispatching two supervisors at the same board concurrently.

pl_bt_debug_connect (PL_DEBUG_REMOTE CONNECT bypass) has the identical thread-context hazard as PL_COMMAND_TAG_CONNECT/START_SCAN/CANCEL_SCAN -- debug_remote.c is polled from main.c's superloop, same thread context. Fixed it too via the same deferred queue, since it shares pl_bt_pending_push/pl_bt_pending_service with the three named call sites.

pl_log_ring_bytes_dropped and pl_log_ring_backlog_hwm are LIFETIME counters, never reset since boot -- a single boot-burst drop pins backlog_hwm at 4095 forever, so post-boot captures cannot show them dropping in absolute terms. The fair comparison is steady-state GROWTH rate, not the raw number.

when reconfiguring the same CMake build dir with different -D flags between a before/after A-B hardware comparison, an intervening git stash pop that lands BEFORE the second reconfigure will silently poison the FIRST (before) build too if you rebuild it again afterward without re-stashing -- CMake's incremental rebuild picks up whatever the working tree currently has. Caught this because both .uf2s came out byte-identical (same MD5) on the first attempt; the fix was rm -rf the build dir and do a full stash/build/pop/build cycle for each variant rather than reusing directories across a flag change.

the interface-4 vendor 'Reset' control transfer (bmRequestType=0x01, bRequest=0x01, wIndex=4, no data) DOES work as a press-free BOOTSEL trigger on this board/Mac when the board's main loop is healthy -- detach_kernel_driver raising EACCES(13) and the ctrl_transfer itself raising USBError errno 5 (I/O Error) are BOTH the success signature, not failures; the board reboots into BOOTSEL regardless. This contradicts the older CLAUDE.md note that this control transfer STALLs -- either the board/tooling changed since pico-link-d74, or that finding was itself an artifact. cdc_sender.py --bootsel is still the simpler path but needs a PL_DEBUG_REMOTE build already flashed; this control transfer works on ANY build.
